html:
The Kaesong Industrial Region was a zone in North Korea, just north of the border near Kaesong, where South Korean companies ran factories with North Korean workers from 2004 to 2016.

It grew out of the Sunshine Policy of engagement of South Korea's president Kim Dae-jung after the 2000 summit with Kim Jong Il. More than a hundred firms made clothes, shoes and parts there, employing over 50,000 North Koreans, whose wages were paid to the North Korean state.

It survived many crises, but in February 2016, after a nuclear test and a rocket launch, South Korea shut it down. In 2020 North Korea blew up the joint liaison office in Kaesong. The zone was the last trace of hopes that trade could ease the division of Korea.
sum: The Kaesong Industrial Region was a zone in North Korea, just north of the border near Kaesong, where South Korean companies ran factories with North Korean workers from 2004 to 2016.
